correctness.rationale: For \(h_\varepsilon=r+\varepsilon u+\varepsilon^2v+o_{C^2}(\varepsilon^2)\) and \(\rho=h+h\prime\prime\), the curvature formula yields \(\Omega_R=\int f_R(\rho)\) and exact area variation forces \(r\int v=-\frac12\int u(u+u\prime\prime)\). Taylor expansion gives the stated \(Q_{R,r}\). Direct differentiation yields \(f_R\prime/f_R=(2R-3r)/(3r(R-r))\), \(f_R\prime\prime/f_R=-2R^2/[9r^2(R-r)^2]\). Orthogonality of Fourier modes gives eigen-coefficients \(C_k=[-f_R\prime\prime-f_R\prime/(r(k^2-1))]/2\); their monotonicity proves sharpness and the transition, while normalized cosine support paths realize every fixed mode with precisely preserved area and valid \(0<\rho<R\). The standard-library finite checker independently reproduced the predicted coefficients and monotonicity; finite quadrature alone is not used as proof.
